draft.title: Perceptual set
card: A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive a stimulus in a particular way. It shapes what we notice and how we interpret it.
Expectation
what we think we will see or taste. A person told a drink is cherry flavoured may taste cherry, even when the flavour is something else.
Context
the setting around a stimulus. The same ambiguous shape can be read as a letter among letters, or as a number among numbers.
Experience and motivation
Past learning makes some interpretations come to mind first. A need or goal, such as hunger, can make us quicker to notice food signs.
draft.remember: Perceptual set means we perceive what we are ready for, shaped by expectation, context, experience and motivation.

a.q: Which best describes a perceptual set?
opts: A readiness to perceive a stimulus in a particular way
The turning of a stimulus into electrical impulses
The detection of a stimulus by a sense receptor
Splitting attention across two tasks at the same time
a.why: A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive in a certain way, shaped by things like expectation and context. Detecting a stimulus with receptors is only sensation, which comes before the brain interprets it.
a.clue: Think of the brain being prepared before it interprets.

b.q: Tariq is very thirsty after a long run. At a busy fair, he quickly spots a drink stall that other people walk past without noticing. Which factor best explains this?
opts: Motivation, as his need for a drink readies him to notice it
Context, as the busy fair changes how the stall looks
Expectation, as he was told the stall would be there
Experience, as he has seen drink stalls at other fairs
b.why: Tariq's thirst is a need that readies him to notice drink stalls, so motivation is the best fit. Experience may play a part, but the case points to his thirst, and nothing says he was told about the stall or that the fair changed how it looked.
b.clue: Look for what Tariq needs right now.

a.best: A readiness to perceive a stimulus in a particular way

b.best: Motivation, as his need for a drink readies him to notice it

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for what Tariq needs right now' echoes the word 'need' in the right option, so a student can match the words and pick the answer without understanding motivation as a perceptual set factor.
